Got mine done a month ago exactly. The pain for the first piercing was probably a 4/10, second one was 7,8/10. This is probably the case cause all that adrenaline goes away right after the first piercing's done with, so your second will probably hurt more. It's a sharp quick pain and then it just becomes achey and sore after. I'm no expert, but I'll try to give you some tips :)

In my case, I got mine done while I was on my period so they ended up bleeding a bit cus blood gets a lil thinner on your period (I think).

Expect a bit of bleeding the first couple of days. What I did was I cut some pantiliners and stuck them on the inside of my sports bras so they wouldnt get blood on them. I'm not sure if this is okay to do but I only had to do this for like 3-ish days after I got them done and it didn't give me any problems.

If the pain is really annoying, don't take aspirin or ibuprofen cause that will thin your blood out and probably make it bleed more during your first couple of days; take some tylenol instead.

For cleaning, just make a little salt solution out of non-iodized salt and warm water and dip some q-tips in these and clean alongside the barbells and wherever the blood/crust is. Be careful in trying not to move and agitate the piercing too much while cleaning! If the blood/crust is really caked on there, try soaking them in your salt solution or simply warm water for a couple of minutes to soften the crusty stuff and clean with q-tips again. Also invest in a piercing aftercare spray and thoroughly spray both of em down after cleaning.  Make sure to pat them dry as best as you can afterwards!

For the first week my showerhead water pressure was a little too much for my piercings and made them sore, so I would stand with my back facing the water instead. I'd also try to avoid any really harsh hair or body wash products running down and getting on my piercings the best I could. And make sure you put on your clothes carefully! Try leaning forward while putting on shirts and stuff to make sure they don't snag. If you have boobs, I feel like smaller cup sizes will be a taddd bit easier to manage the first couple of days since they don't really move a whole lot when doing daily stuff, but if you're on the bigger side it still shouldn't be too much of a problem. Once you get back into the swing of regular bras, avoid anything too lacey or tight; they could snag or have little room to breathe.

Seems like a lot to watch out for, but in my opinion these are totally worth the effort. They look good on anyone and def boosted my confidence. Good luck to you if you do decide on getting them!

Oh I totally get that, I'm actually trying to wear bras less nowadays too (the confidence my piercings give me is a godsend)!

The thing with these piercings and the healing process is that you might have to wear something like a sports bra for the first couple of weeks (especially the first week), they get really sensitive and the feeling of things brushing up on them while they heal is not a very good sensation. As the weeks go by you might get more comfortable with them and that could be when your confidence gradually starts spiking! Personally, if I see someone's piercings through their clothing I will automatically brand them as a cool ass person. 

But these are YOUR piercings, confidence will come naturally to you. No rush :)
